transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

For months I’ve felt unusually ‘up’ and on edge all the time, like my mood is cranked way higher than normal and I can’t dial it back. It just feels like I'm constantly wired and I don't know how to slow myself down.
When you feel 'up' and wired, do you also feel unusually happy, euphoric, or irritable — and have you had periods where your mood was so high that it led to risky behavior or trouble at work or home?

Yes, I feel a mix of intense euphoria where I talk a mile a minute about my ideas, but I also flip on a dime and snap at my students and partner over tiny things. It has caused massive trouble—my lab is in complete chaos with missed deadlines and student complaints, my department chair has warned me about my job security, and at home, my partner is exhausted and finds me impossible to be around.
Have you ever had periods of low mood, depression, or loss of energy that lasted for several days or more, coming after or before these 'up' and wired phases?

No, I haven't really experienced those low or depressed periods, at least not recently. For the past seven months, it has been almost entirely this continuous, wired, and high-energy state without any downs.
Have you gone for more than a week without needing sleep or feeling the need to rest, while still feeling energetic and mentally active?

Yes, that's been going on for about seven months now where I only sleep two or three hours a night. I wake up buzzing with energy and ideas, pacing around making notes at 3 a.m. without feeling tired at all. It's actually frustrating because my body just can't keep up with how fast my mind is racing.
Have your symptoms been present almost every day for most of the day, without a clear break, for the past seven months?

Yes, absolutely, it has been a non-stop, everyday experience for the past seven months, starting right when I got the big grant and took over the new lab. It feels like there is absolutely no 'off' switch and I am constantly wired. It's incredibly frustrating because I just can't get a single moment of peace.

Have you ever had a distinct period lasting at least four days where your mood was abnormally and persistently elevated or irritable, clearly different from your usual non-depressed mood, before age 25?
I don't recall having any episodes like this back when I was under 25. These issues really only started about seven months ago when everything at the lab ramped up.

Have you ever had a distinct period lasting at least one week where you were so energized, talkative, or irritable that it was noticeable to others, even if you didn’t need much sleep or seemed unusually productive?

Yes, that describes exactly what I've been experiencing for the past seven months. I've been constantly wired, talking rapidly, and snapping at others while sleeping only two or three hours a night and constantly starting new projects. It has been incredibly noticeable to my partner, students, and colleagues, and it's causing a massive amount of strain.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was F31, and based on this conversation, F31 remains the most consistent diagnosis. The patient describes a persistent and abnormally elevated, irritable, and expansive mood with increased energy, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, and significant impairment in social and occupational functioning lasting over seven months. These symptoms meet the duration and severity criteria for a manic episode (F31), particularly given the continuous nature of symptoms for more than one week and clear functional impairment. The absence of a prior history of depressive episodes does not rule out bipolar disorder, as a single manic episode is sufficient for diagnosis. No features suggest a better fit, and no other differential diagnoses (e.g., F30, F32, or F43) are more consistent with the clinical picture.
